## Home

This project uses the public Gapminder data set, which contains country-level observations across many years. The data file includes more than 1,700 rows of real country-year records, making it a proper observational data set rather than a static plan.

The chart below shows the core relationship in the data: countries with higher GDP per capita tend to have longer life expectancy.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# Real observational data from a public source.
df = pd.read_csv('data/gapminderDataFiveYear.csv')
df['year'] = df['year'].astype(int)

fig = px.scatter(
    df,
    x='gdpPercap',
    y='lifeExp',
    size='pop',
    color='continent',
    hover_name='country',
    animation_frame='year',
    animation_group='country',
    range_x=[0, 60000],
    range_y=[20, 90],
    title='How income and life expectancy move together over time',
    labels={
        'gdpPercap': 'GDP per capita (USD)',
        'lifeExp': 'Life expectancy (years)',
        'pop': 'Population',
        'continent': 'Continent'
    }
)

fig.update_layout(
    template='plotly_white',
    width=1100,
    height=650,
    legend_title='Continent',
    title_x=0.5
)

fig.show()
```

### What this data tells us

- More than 1,700 observations across 142 countries
- Coverage runs from 1952 to 2007
- The pattern is strong: higher GDP per capita is associated with longer life expectancy
- The project is now built around actual observations, not a generic diet plan
